items.name: Japan AI Appropriateness Guideline
items.description: Guideline for Ensuring the Appropriateness of Research, Development and Utilization of AI-Related Technology (AI Strategic Headquarters decision under Art. 13 of the AI Basic Act): voluntary, principle-based guidance for all stakeholders

sections.text: Positioning, elements to consider, basic policies

requirements.text: Organisations should take measures at a level appropriate to their position and to the AI's characteristics and risks, weighing the guideline's ten elements - human-centredness, fairness, safety, transparency, accountability, security, privacy and personal information, fair competition, AI literacy and innovation - under its four basic policies: risk-based approach, stakeholder involvement, end-to-end governance and agile PDCA.
requirements.rationale: The guideline deliberately fixes no absolute level of appropriateness; the elements and policies are the structured way an organisation shows it looked at the right things.

controls.description: Record how each of the ten elements was weighed for AI systems in deployment, sized to their risk.
Apply the four basic policies as standing criteria when approving AI projects and revisiting them in the PDCA cycle.

titles.text: Items for research and business entities

sections.text: Ensuring appropriateness holistically through AI governance

requirements.text: Entities that develop or use AI should build, operate and continuously improve AI governance across the whole lifecycle - design, development, provision and implementation - with processes to identify, evaluate and treat risk, monitoring and evaluation with management involvement, appropriate information disclosure, and education and training.
requirements.rationale: Lifecycle-wide governance with management visibility is the guideline's central ask of providers; existing IT governance may be leveraged rather than rebuilt.

controls.description: Stand up an AI governance process spanning the lifecycle with named management accountability and a periodic review cadence.
Maintain AI risk-identification and treatment registers with evidence of management review, and run role-appropriate AI education and training.

requirements.text: Providers should ensure transparency to build trust - reasonable explainability of training-data provenance and outputs, and disclosure of an AI system's mechanics, limits, prohibited uses, data-collection policy and output-reliability cautions when providing it - secure sufficient safety through technical means such as defences against misjudgement and hallucination, maintain a safe environment through business-continuity measures, and show consideration for stakeholders such as data holders.
requirements.rationale: These are the provider-side items the applicability rules group as transparency-and-safety: what an organisation tells stakeholders and how it keeps the system dependable.

controls.description: Publish user-facing documentation of system mechanics, limits, prohibited uses and data handling for each AI service offered.
Apply technical safety measures proportionate to identified failure modes - including misjudgement and hallucination defences - and cover AI-dependent processes in continuity planning.
